findings.message: The check treats every folder on the PR head that isn't on the base tip as added by the PR (`added = headDirs.filter(d => !base.has(d))`). Round 2 handled folders the PR removed or renamed. It missed the opposite case: main renames or removes a folder after the branch was cut. The PR branch still carries that folder unchanged from the merge base, so the check counts it as added. It then fails the PR for a number reuse the PR didn't make, and that the merge would not produce. This is likely to happen, because the script itself says the known pairs on main (062, 074, 075) are to be renumbered there. Fix: count a folder as added only if it is on head and not in the merge base. Also drop folders that are in the merge base but no longer on base (main removed them) from `after`. Add the case to the table test.
findings.scenario: mergeBase = [074-dev-demo-data, 074-fork-pr-review-gate]. Main then renumbers 074-fork-pr-review-gate to 090-fork-pr-review-gate: base = [074-dev-demo-data, 090-fork-pr-review-gate]. The PR only adds 089-mine: head = [074-dev-demo-data, 074-fork-pr-review-gate, 089-mine]. check() reports '074-fork-pr-review-gate: number 074 is already used by 074-dev-demo-data' and CI fails, though the merged tree has no duplicate.

findings.message: A number reaches the duplicate map either because the client flagged it or because two dirs share it within one push. When the client flagged it, only that push's dirs are listed. In a CI batch of more than 200 changes the two folders can fall in different batches, so the skip line reads 'two changes numbered 074: 074-a' and names one folder. The person can't tell which other folder collides. Fix: when only one dir is known, word the line differently (for example 'another change also uses 074'), or have the reader send the colliding dir names.
findings.scenario: main has 210 changes, and 074-a and 074-b land in different batches. Each batch's skip line names only its own folder.

findings.message: The self-sync calls planWithdrawals with `refs: null`, on the claim that it "reads main and every specclaw branch at once, so any ref counts". But readSpecclaw only takes an overlay folder that already exists on main (`byDir.has(d) || archived`). A change that exists only on a specclaw/* branch is never read, so it is never in `named`. A proposal that a 062 branch push created for that change (meta.source `specclaw/090-x@…`) is eligible, and any self-sync of a main commit newer than the branch commit withdraws it. Fix: limit refs to the refs the self-sync actually read in full (main), or treat every overlay's folders as read for its ref.
findings.scenario: A developer pushes specclaw/090-x, which creates FLT-090 with source specclaw/090-x@abc and synced_commit_at 10:00. A later merge to main at 11:00 runs `sync:specclaw --overlay <090-x branch>`. The overlay's 090-x folder is not on main, so it isn't read. planWithdrawals(refs=null) withdraws FLT-090 while the change is still in progress.
